10.1002_aenm.71238: The electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 RR) offers a promising route for sustainable ammonia synthesis. Due to the interfacial synergistic effects, Cu–Co catalysts exhibit outstanding activity. However, the underlying evolution of active sites remains poorly understood, which induces the reported advantageous phase‐segregating in situ restructuring. By monitoring Co(OH) 2 /Cu catalysts, our observations revealed that Cu‐ and Co‐related sites undergo dynamic, “seesaw‐like” reciprocal reactivation instead of mutual stabilization. In situ SERS, DMPO‐EPR and DFT calculations show that this process is driven by the competing oxidative/reductive forces under NO 3 RR conditions, which cause site deactivation, and mediated via the transfer of ∙O/∙OH and H* radicals across interfaces. Critically, these radicals trigger the conversion of deactivated CuO x and Co(OH) 2 sites into highly active oxide‐derived Cu 0 and CoOOH, respectively. As the interfacial transfer of radicals constitutes an irreversible process, the observed in situ restructuring is inherently rationalized. This conjugated, seesaw‐like mechanism accelerates a dynamic, self‐regulating redox balance at Cu–Co heterointerface, continuously enhancing the synergy between Cu‐ and Co‐related sites and the overall NO 3 RR performance. Beyond catalyst development, this work offers a mechanistic framework for understanding how competing oxidative and reductive forces are redistributed at heterointerfaces, providing guiding principles for the rational design of next‐generation electrocatalysts.
10.1002_aenm.71502: Refrigeration Electrochemically driven dissolution–crystallization refrigeration couples the endothermic dissolution of redox-active salts with electrochemical regeneration. As depicted on the cover, regenerated crystals dissolve in the foreground cooling reservoir to absorb heat, while the electrolyte circulates through the electrochemical cell for recrystallization and reuse. Spatially separating cooling from electrochemical regeneration minimizes direct interference from Joule heating. More in article number e71304, Pei Liu, Jia Li, Jiangjiang Duan, and co-workers.
10.1016_j.jece.2026.125143: In recent years, the rapid growth in lithium-ion battery (LIB) production has led to a sharp increase in spent LIBs, creating growing pressure on critical metal resources and environmental management. As a result, the development of efficient and environmentally friendly recycling technologies has become increasingly urgent. Conventional recycling strategies, mainly hydrometallurgy and pyrometallurgy, often suffer from high energy consumption, intensive chemical use, complex process flows, secondary pollution, and limited selectivity for valuable metals. In comparison, electrochemical methods enable the selective oxidation or reduction of target metal species through precise control of the applied potential or current density. By using electrochemically supplied electrons to drive or regenerate redox reactions, these methods may reduce the use of externally added acids, bases, or reducing agents in selected process configurations. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in electrochemical leaching and electrodeposition for recycling spent LIB cathode materials. Particular attention is given to leaching classifications, stepwise metal dissolution behavior, thermodynamic considerations, and the key challenges of selective recovery and scale-up in practical applications.
10.1039_d6ta00035e: A vdW Cs 3 YSr 3 I 12 /monolayer GaN dual-semiconductor heterojunction is designed, where the NEA at the Y/GaN(0001) interface suppresses gap states, achieving zero-barrier quasi-ohmic contact and reaching a tunneling efficiency of 97.1% ( S = 0.74).
